children: announced Monday it has entered into a definitive agreement to sell its Microfluidics business to ARCHIMED, an investment firm focused exclusively on healthcare industries.

The transaction is expected to close in approximately 30 days, subject to customary closing conditions. Until closing, the Microfluidics business will continue to operate as part of Standard BioTools, the company highlighted.

Michael Egholm, PhD, President and Chief Executive Officer of Standard BioTools, said, “ARCHIMED brings deep healthcare and life sciences expertise, a strong understanding of the market, and the resources to support the business’ next chapter. This is a strong outcome for our employees and our customers, and we believe the business will continue to grow and innovate under new ownership. This transaction marks another important step in the strategic actions we laid out for Standard BioTools and our shareholders.”

title: Standard BioTools to sell Microfluidics business to ARCHIMED
